title: What's Your Name?
objective: Ask and answer What's your name? with I'm… / My name is…, using Nice to meet you.
intro_md:
[L1: In this lesson you learn to ask someone's name and to give yours with 'I'm…' and 'My name is…'. You also learn 'Nice to meet you.' — what you say the first time you meet someone.]
{{l1_contrast:copula_be}}
notes: TODO_audio: exercises 2, 7, 8 carry the spoken line as written transcript in the prompt; audio assets not yet produced. Band map: U1 ai_written lesson is L03/L17 (controlled dialogue completion) — ex 9 is that slot for L03.

exercises.prompt: nice · meet · What's your name? · My name is… · I'm… · Nice to meet you.
exercises.rationale: Establish form-meaning link with audio for both answer frames and the meeting formula before any production.

exercises.prompt: [audio] 'Hello! What's your name?' — [L1: What is the speaker doing?]
exercises.rationale: Function discrimination among this lesson's chunks and L01 farewells: the reply depends on recognizing a question for a name, not on catching every word.

options.label: What's your name?
options.rationale: The question asks for a name.

options.label: Nice to meet you.
options.rationale: Also said at first meetings — forces listening for the question form, not the situation.

options.label: Goodbye!
options.rationale: A farewell; catches learners who answer from the greeting 'Hello' without processing the question.

exercises.prompt: [L1: Match each line to the best reply.]
exercises.rationale: Adjacency pairs: each opener has a conventional reply. Recycles L01 greetings/farewells beside the new chunks so the four functions stay distinct.

exercises.prompt: A: ___ your name?  B: I'm Sara.
exercises.rationale: Targets the question word: es '¿Cómo te llamas?' transfers as 'How is your name?' — 'How's' is the L1-predicted error; 'Who's' asks about a third person.
Assembles the full answer frame; feedback highlights that 'my' comes before 'name' and that 'is' cannot be dropped (zero-copula L1s predictably omit it).

exercises.prompt: A: Nice to ___ you!  B: Nice to meet you, ___.
exercises.rationale: Chunk integrity plus the echo reply. 'see' is the diagnostic distractor: es 'conocer/ver' overlap makes 'Nice to see you' feel right, but it is for people you already know.

exercises.prompt: [audio] 'Hi! I'm Tom.' — [L1: What is a good reply?]
exercises.rationale: Trains the whole first-meeting routine as a move sequence: after a self-introduction, the reply greets back and uses the meeting formula.

options.label: Hi, Tom! Nice to meet you.
options.rationale: Greets back and closes the first-meeting pair.

options.label: Goodbye, Tom!
options.rationale: A farewell in an opening slot — function confusion recycled from L01.

options.label: What's my name?
options.rationale: my/your pronoun flip — a frequent early error when chunks are memorized without the pronoun analyzed.

exercises.prompt: [audio] 'What's your name?' → [L1: Answer with your real name, then spell it.]
asr_focus: 'is' present in the frame (zero-copula L1 check)
exercises.rationale: Personalized production chaining L03's frame with L02's spelling — the exact sequence used on forms and phones.

exercises.prompt: [L1: You meet a new classmate. Greet them, exchange names, use 'Nice to meet you.', and say goodbye.]
exercises.rationale: Controlled dialogue completion (band map: U1 ai_written slot at L03); integrates L01 greetings with both L03 name frames in real time and counts toward guided-interaction minutes.
